🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE Seeks $1 Billion From Investors to Expand the Grid</u>

The CFE plans to raise about $1 billion through CFE Capital, letting investors buy into the income of its public transmission lines, El Financiero reports. Officials will meet investors in New York in early November, with the offering expected before Thanksgiving. The goal: grow the transmission network about 7% this administration and triple recent investment levels over the next two years. It would be Mexico's largest share offering since February 2020, and the lines stay in public hands.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>INEGI: All Eight Measured Edomex Cities Feel Safer Under Delfina Gómez</u>

INEGI's urban security survey for the third quarter of 2026 shows the perception of insecurity fell in all eight State of Mexico municipalities it measures, compared with September 2025. Tlalnepantla led with a 26.1% annual drop. In 2023 the PRI handed over a state it had governed since 1929.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Under Córdova, the INE Also Paid the "Coyote" Network</u>

Between 2018 and 2023 the INE and state electoral bodies signed more than 1 billion pesos in contracts with companies tied to the Hernández Casillas brothers, firms with no offices and no employees. Contralínea found at least four INE contracts with the network under Lorenzo Córdova, including INE/ADQ-0022/15 to Cartonera Plástica: it started at 9.8 million pesos and ended above 11 million. Sources say ASF auditors are only requesting records from Taddei's short tenure.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The UIF Froze INE Contractors for Money Laundering. Judges Unfroze Them.</u>

Companies that won INE contracts were placed on the Financial Intelligence Unit's blocked-persons list over suspected money laundering, former UIF head Pablo Gómez revealed. Judges then granted them provisional suspensions. "They have no industrial plant, they don't manufacture anything, they aren't even merchants... they're intermediaries who win the contracts and then go to the print shops," Gómez said. His word for them: "authentic coyotes."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Ships Its First Pork Products to the Philippines</u>

After negotiations that began in 2017, Mexico's first pork shipment to the Philippines has left Yucatán: 22 tonnes from Kekén's TIF 712 plant, bound for North Manila. The deal also opens the door to beef and pork meat and offal from federally inspected plants. The Philippines, with 114 million people, expects to consume 1.9 million tonnes of pork in 2027.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Congress Moves to Cut 5 Billion Pesos From the INE and Send It to Schools</u>

The Chamber of Deputies' budget committee proposes trimming the INE's 2027 budget from 42.27 to 37.28 billion pesos, after the institute asked for 47 billion. The 5 billion would go to schools (3 billion for La Escuela es Nuestra), the environment (1 billion), civil aviation (700 million) and the search for disappeared persons (300 million). Same week the INE's president resigned over contracts with printing "coyotes."

🇲🇽🏭 "The estimates were that we would not exceed 1% annually, and that if we exceeded 1% it would be a lot. And I always said: they are not counting the public works and the housing we are building." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apaseo el Grande, Guanajuato Inspecting the Querétaro–Irapuato passenger train on October 31, she cited INEGI's new figure: the economy grew 3.2% annually in the third quarter. She said the train and housing programs are the public works driving the economy most, close to 1% of GDP this year, along with private investment in Querétaro and Guanajuato. The 102 km section, with stations in Apaseo, Celaya, Cortazar-Villagrán, Salamanca and Irapuato, is 25% complete and employs 3,365 people directly and 5,700 indirectly. On the two opposition governors present: "We are from different political parties, but that has nothing to do with it when we work together for the good of Mexico."

🇲🇽🎨 "Where do young people have to be? In the street or in school? In school. Well then, we have to build more schools." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Celaya, Guanajuato She said the best way to reduce crime is building more schools, "and of course police, prosecutors, everything that has to be there." She and Guanajuato governor Libia Dennise García agreed on two priorities: first scholarships, second more schools. 90 secondary schools in the state are being converted to also run as high schools in the afternoon shift, 13 new Margarita Maza high schools with cultural and sports activities are under construction, and the new CBETIS 308 campus in Celaya opens in March. The goal: practically every secondary graduate able to enter a free, quality high school.

🇲🇽🚆 "It is the rescue of the passenger train. The passenger train has great virtues: it is faster than the car... it connects regional development that otherwise could not be connected." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Polotitlán, State of Mexico Supervising the Mexico City–Querétaro train on October 31, she said the line is 32% built with 90% of the right-of-way secured. This administration is building about 2,500 km of rail: Tren Maya freight, completion of the Interoceanic, and new passenger lines Mexico City–Pachuca, Mexico City–Querétaro–Nuevo Laredo and Querétaro–Guadalajara, an investment of nearly 700 billion pesos. In some areas the trains will work like urban rail for daily commuters. Army engineers are building the line, and the Defense Ministry makes the railroad ties.

🇲🇽🎨 "Education is not a privilege for those who can pay for it. Education is a right for all Mexicans." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Celaya, Guanajuato In Celaya on October 31 she said all public schools up to high school must be free: "Not a single cent should be charged." After asking the mothers at the CBETIS whether they paid fees, she announced the school is free starting tomorrow, with the government covering what the fees used to pay for. Forty years ago she joined a movement for free higher education: "So with even more reason, being president, we have to advance in quality, public and free education." "For many years they told us that private schools were better than public ones. True or not? Well, it is not true."
